newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Italy's Prodi arrives in Albanian port of Vlores.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi arrives in Albanian port of Vlores.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi arrived in Vlore on Sunday for a meeting with his Albanian counterpart, Bashkim Fino, witnesses said.

Fino was on hand to greet Prodi at a wide open space 10 km (six miles) outside the southern port city, they said. Prodi planned to arrive last week, but a new outbreak of violence prompted Fino to urge postponement of the meeting in Vlore, which has been under rebel control since the start of an armed uprising.
Prodi arrived in a helicopter that was escorted by two other heavily weaponed Italian helicopters. About two dozen armed Italian marines were on the ground waiting for Prodi when he landed.

Albanian Prime Minister Fino had arrived by helicopter about 10 minutes earlier. Fino's helicopter was escorted by two Albanian army helicopters. There were also dozens of Vlore police officers, armed with Kalashnikov rifles, on hand.

Prodi, who will fly later to the capital, Tirana, had paid a brief visit to Gjirokaster, also in the south, on April 2. He was the first foreign leader to visit Albania since the spasm of lawless violence swept the country following the collapse of get-rich- quick schemes wiped out the life savings of many Albanians.

Prodi had expressed his condolences at that brief meeting to Fino for the sinking of a refugee ship off Italy on March 28 in which about 80 refugees died. It was the worst maritime disaster in modern Albanian history.
